mechanism_narrative: A high level of residential housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The relationship is positive and consistent across historical data.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return correlation with HOUST level is negative (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.5%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI (CPIAUCSL) creates a predictive signal: when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% and CPIAUCSL is rising above 2.0% annually, it indicates a low-rate, moderate-inflation environment that supports positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.0% annualized) is met in more than 50% of cases, but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 8%), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the economy is perceived to be in a recessionary phase.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE > 8%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it indicates high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks tighten policy.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (annualized), the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is positive and consistent across historical data.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return correlation with INDPRO level is negative (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between labor market strength (PAYEMS) and housing demand (HOUST) creates a predictive signal: when PAYEMS is above 134000 and HOUST is above 700, it indicates a robust economy with strong consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (PAYEMS > 134000 AND HOUST > 700) is met in more than 50% of cases, but the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of those cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In low housing demand regimes (HOUST < 600), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as the economy is perceived to be in a slowdown phase.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST < 600, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
